A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReasonVQA benchmark and construction framework. Their main text, tables, figures, mathematical content, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, dataset analyses, and a 1,000-pair user study, with supplementary results in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and additionally reports answer-correctness judgments, GPT-4o multiple-choice results, and domain-level performance analysis.

M1.justification: The construction pipeline and Appendix Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 3.2.1 newly mentions developing linguistic variants for each template, but the template-bank counts and examples remain identical. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents a procedural addition or previously undocumented implementation detail.

E1.justification: The image sources, ReasonVQA variants, knowledge domains, and open-ended and multiple-choice tasks remain unchanged, as do the evaluated external benchmarks. INFOSEEK and Encyclopedic VQA are added only to the descriptive dataset comparison, without reported model evaluations on them.

E2.justification: GPT-4o is added to the multiple-choice comparison in Table 2 and the corresponding panel of v3 Figure 6; v1 included it only in the open-ended comparison. The other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: The reported user-study protocol adds answer-correctness assessment to naturalness and grammatical-error judgments, retaining 20 participants and 1,000 question-image pairs. The existing evaluation metrics and dataset split remain unchanged. The newly described hop-proportional sampling clarifies an existing size experiment rather than establishing that it was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix Section 3.2 and Figure 10 add a diagnostic breakdown of accuracy across knowledge domains and identify difficult numerical questions. The user study also adds factual-error assessment. Existing analyses by hop count, scene-graph availability, image source, and dataset size are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix Tables 3 and 4 retain identical SD and SEM reporting and values. Neither version reports additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds GPT-4o multiple-choice scores of 76.6 on ReasonVQA-U, 73.4 on ReasonVQA-B, and 96.7 on OK-VQA, plus subgroup results. It also reports 96% answer correctness and domain averages including 20.7% for Health & Medicine and 22.5% for Art & Creative Expressions. Shared benchmark and fine-tuning scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph-based construction description, recursive pseudocode, and numerical distractor-generation formula are retained. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a large knowledge-based multi-hop VQA benchmark, inexpensive scalable construction, and substantial difficulty for current models. The revised conclusion condenses these claims without changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 identifies numerical facts and ambiguous measurements, such as construction heights or lengths, as principal sources of incorrect dataset answers. This adds a substantive qualification to dataset reliability beyond v1's naturalness and grammar discussion. Existing interpretations of model difficulty and dataset-size trends remain.

D1.justification: Appendix Section 3.1 newly specifies random proportional sampling from one-, two-, and three-hop pools for the existing dataset-size experiment. Section 4.2 clarifies that fine-tuning uses image-question-answer inputs. Code-access information is unchanged; these disclosures do not establish retraining or dataset regeneration.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Table 1 add INFOSEEK and Encyclopedic VQA, discussing their annotation costs and human quality-control requirements. This modestly broadens comparison with knowledge-based VQA datasets while retaining the paper's existing research positioning.

P1.justification: Several passages on template generation, scalability, metrics, and conclusions are rewritten or shortened. Domain explanation is moved into the main text, and appendix experiments are reorganized into dataset-size and dataset-aspect subsections. Author and affiliation text also change, but the overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the domain-accuracy chart and expands the multiple-choice results display. The dataset-size plots move from main Figure 6 to appendix Figure 9 and merge into one chart with solid and dashed lines. The existing domain-distribution chart is also reproduced in the main text, and Tables 1 and 2 gain rows.

improvement.justification: Answer-correctness validation, domain-level diagnostics, and the sampling explanation strengthen evidence and reproducibility beyond v1's naturalness-focused study and less-documented size experiment. The gains are limited rather than transformative. The unchanged claim of an order-of-magnitude size advantage also remains problematic: v3 Table 1 lists 4.2M questions for ReasonVQA versus 1.35M for INFOSEEK.
